items.title: A generic function returning `dyn Pipe>` built from `value.derive(\|v\| v)` is refused natively — "the `rust` backend does not emit a value of an unbound generic type parameter (parameter 1 of `pipe_of`) yet" — while the same body at a concrete type builds and runs; it is why a mirrored store's `states()` (and any `TransientSource::states()` over a generic) does not build natively
items.body:
Repro: `sweeps/order50/store-50/finds/generic-dyn-pipe-native/main.vl` — `fun pipe_of

(value: dyn Source>): dyn Pipe> { let pipe: dyn Pipe> = value.derive(|v| v); pipe }`, called at `P = str` and observed with `effect`: JS prints `-` then `x`; `vilan run --backend rust` refuses at the call. The same function written at `str` builds and prints the same on both backends (the `combine` form too). Met building A153 S2's `RemoteStoreSome::states()` (`impl RemoteStoreSome with TransientSource` in `std::rpc::mirror`, whose pipes are `combine((leased, told)).derive(..)`): the JS pin is `reactive_channels::a153_s2_a_remote_handle_tells_pending_ready_absent_and_failed_through_states`; the native differential probe leaves `states()` out until this is fixed (it should then gain one). Likely the dyn-pipe construction's closure types are not substituted at the instance. Sizing S–M; vilan-rust / mono.

items.title: A mirrored store's handle as a `dyn Source` is refused natively — "the `rust` backend does not emit `attach_observer` through a `dyn` object on `RemoteStoreSome_…` (the implementation takes 3 parameters where the declaration takes 5) yet" — so `let motd: dyn Source<Option<str>> = g.motd()` builds and runs on JS only; a plain user struct implementing `Source` the same way builds
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order50/store-50/finds/remote-face-as-dyn-source-native/main.vl` (a mirrored `Store<Global>` over an in-process pair; the client's `g.motd()` as `dyn Source<Option<str>>`, observed with `effect`). Pre-existing on next @5fe24f86 (checked with that tree's std). A user struct whose `Source` impl forwards to a cell the same way builds natively, so the difference is the hidden context parameters: the trait method's declaration carries two (some impl of `attach_observer` in the program reads a context) and `RemoteStoreSome`'s impl carries none, and the native object table does not pad the call. It also stands in the way of `states()` natively (its pipe takes the handle as a `dyn Source`), beside B605. Sizing S; vilan-rust's dyn tables.

items.discussion: store-50 (Order 50); sweeps/order50/store-50/kolt-mirror-v0.48.0.patch; C3b (incr-49) narrowed the mirror seed; R-f the std-prefix paper; A149 S5
items.title: kolt over the mirrored store (A153 S5's exhibit) checks with +7.0% inferences (134,799 → 144,180) and +8.9% attempts, the server leg's first checks phase ~+16% CPU, while kolt's OWN declarations get cheaper (server leg 24,357 → 21,495 work units, client leg 524,124 → 504,981): the growth is std's — `std::rpc::mirror` loads again once a service returns a `Store`, which C3b had kept out of kolt
items.body: Measured on the scratch copies under the store-50 tip (same compiler for both): `VILAN_COUNTERS` inferences 134,799 → 144,180, attempts 31,017 → 33,764, peak heap within noise (158-160 → 161-165 MB); `--explain-cost` shows the user package's work units falling on both legs (the deleted `get_*` stubs and memo plumbing outweigh the derive-written `StoreWire` walkers for `Global`, `ChannelRecord` and `User`, ~2,900 units of the server leg's 21,495). So A149 S5 (compiler-generated store nodes) is NOT the measured need — the derive text is ~13% of the server leg's own cost and the leg got cheaper overall; the cost is std's mirror module (1,400+ lines, loaded per C3b's rule whenever a service returns a store), which incr-49 measured at about +5% of a kolt keystroke. Doors: (a) the std-prefix paper (R-f, papers-50) — a persisted, prefix-analyzed std makes this growth free on a keystroke; (b) split `std::rpc::mirror` into server and client halves loaded per leg. Rec: (a), and re-measure E121's seven rows with the exhibit applied at the seal. Sizing S (measurement); the fix is R-f's.
